angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened): each rusher's tracked Combine 40 start laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts on one clock (combine_frames vs game_frames_sample); per-player Carry-over and the NFL first step tested against pressure beyond a no-tracking forecast in one continuous leave-one-class-out test, plus a within-rusher snap-level mechanism test.
metric_name: First step = mean speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement; Carry-over = NFL first step minus Combine 40 first step, each in sd after weight and EDGE share
headline_number: After size the 40 start previews the NFL first step at rho 0.07 (n = 67). Held-out slope with the forecast as offset: Carry-over +0.2 pts per sd [-0.1, 0.5], shuffle p 0.48 (n = 52); NFL first step +0.8 [0.1, 1.4], positive in 3 of 3 classes, shuffle p 0.01, best-of-11-windows p 0.02, but 2025 alone +0.4 [-0.6, 1.4]. Within rusher, snap by snap: OR 1.49 [1.25, 1.77] per sd on 1,279 random rushes (120 pressures), 1.51 with snap NGS get-off, sideways, down and alignment controls.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_10/cand_3 (8.15) applying the round-10 judges' top_changes. (1) The hit-count test is replaced by one continuous out-of-class test: per-class quasi-binomial slope with the out-of-class no-tracking forecast as a logit offset, random-effects shrinkage pooling, a 2,000-shuffle within-class null, and a best-of-11-windows adjusted p printed next to the headline; the same test is run on the Combine 40 start, Carry-over and the NFL first step (Table 1, Fig 2B). (2) New lower-variance mechanism test from the game frames: within-rusher snap-level pressure on the same sampled snap, with snap NGS get-off, sideways share, passing down and alignment controls, per class and per role (Fig 4). (3) Rule frozen in frozen_rule.json with a sha256 prefix quoted in the text. (4) Lede rewritten without brackets or jargon; mid-p, Fisher and 27-cell grid removed from the body. (5) Fig 1 is now a six-player small multiple (two plus hits, two plus misses, two minus flags) with pressure-minus-forecast 80% intervals and pressures/rushes per row. (6) The old Fig 4 (hit counts + grid heatmap) is dropped; the grid survives as one appendix row. (7) Decision card gives per-player actions, team, a sideways (stunt/slant scheme) percentile, and 'at stake' pressures per season = cost of a wrong call; the Gillotte/Umanmielen pair gets a scheme reading. (8) 'So what for a team' replaces 'What a team can do'; the power statement moved to Limitations. (9) One sample-flow table reconciles 85/67/69/52 rushers and 1,563/1,279 starts. 4 figures + 3 tables; 1,780 words by check.py (about 1,900 by wc).
open_risks: The angle's question (does translation explain production beyond pick?) is still answered with a null; the positive evidence is for the in-game first step, not the Combine
The clean 2025 class alone is weak (+0.4 pts per sd, one-sided p 0.26) and one new class has only 47% power at the pooled slope
The snap-level link may run partly from the play to the start (free rushes, slides away); there are no blockers in the sample, and the sideways control only partly addresses stunts
Season NGS get-off already ranks pressure at 0.40 and the first step adds 0.12 beyond it (p 0.33), so for clubs with NGS the season-level use is a tiebreak
The 0.3-0.5 s window was read off the payoff curve in an earlier round; the best-of-11 adjustment (p 0.02) covers windows, not the five-group screen
